description: 30 realistic cafe preference rules for ceiling eval — 10 structural-hard, 10 structural-soft, 10 semantic-soft

rules.ruleText: Level 1 (L1) staff must always be paired with a Level 2 (L2) or Manager on the same shift for supervision
No staff member may work more than 6 consecutive days without a rest day
Minimum 10 hours rest between the end of one shift and the start of the next
At least one chef must be scheduled during every kitchen-open slot
Full-time staff must be scheduled for at least 2 weekend shifts per week
No staff member may be scheduled for both opening (before 10:00) and closing (after 20:00) on the same day
Part-time staff may not exceed 25 hours per week
A minimum of 2 baristas must be on shift at all times during operating hours
No staff member may be scheduled for more than 10 hours in a single day
Staff on approved leave must not be scheduled for any shifts during their leave period
During peak lunch period (11:30-14:00), prioritise having more staff on shift
During peak dinner period (18:00-20:30), prioritise having more staff on shift
Prefer scheduling senior (L2) staff during peak hours for better customer service
Avoid scheduling the same staff member for closing shift followed by opening shift the next day
Pair newer (L1) baristas with experienced (L2) baristas when possible for mentoring
Weekend shifts should have at least one more staff member than weekday minimums
Prefer giving part-time staff consistent shift times across the week
Avoid scheduling more than 3 L1 staff together without an L2 present
Prefer keeping morning shifts (before 12:00) staffed by the same team throughout the week for continuity
Try to schedule at least one staff member who worked the previous day's closing shift for the next day's opening, for handover continuity
Distribute weekend shifts fairly across all staff — no one should have significantly more weekend work than others
Rotate closing shifts evenly — avoid repeatedly assigning the same person to close
Give L1 staff exposure to different shift types (morning, lunch, dinner) for learning breadth
Balance total hours across staff of the same employment type to avoid burnout
Prefer not to schedule the same two people together every single shift — vary team composition
When possible, honour staff time-of-day preferences (e.g., some prefer mornings, others evenings)
Distribute the least desirable shifts (early mornings, late nights) equitably rather than loading them onto junior staff
Where schedules are tight, prioritise filling coverage gaps over soft preferences
Avoid giving any single staff member all the public-holiday shifts in a month — rotate holiday coverage
Consider staff commute constraints — prefer assigning staff to shifts that start/end within their stated availability windows rather than right at the boundary
